R1.description: One authoritative semantic version source drives the wheel metadata, workflow-controller --version and every recorded runtime identity

R2.description: The distributable wheel carries the complete runtime (including GENERATION.json) and an explicit build identity (version, source commit, dirty flag, package digest, build origin, release tag)

R3.description: A non-editable wheel/pipx runtime runs inspect, step and worker launch without git, without a source checkout and without direct_url.json; the reproduced git-archive failure is a regression case

R4.description: Runtime identity distinguishes source from package runtimes, is stable when the source checkout changes or disappears, and is recorded in job records, identity.json, status and --version

R5.description: Editable/source execution keeps its commit/worktree snapshot semantics and fail-closed dirty handling

R6.description: Install, verify, upgrade and rollback procedures are documented

R7.description: CI runs Controller shards and frozen conformance suites as parallel, hermetic ubuntu-latest matrix jobs with fail-fast false, and ordinary same-workflow same-ref runs cancel older in-progress runs

R8.description: The release pipeline publishes only after all validation passes, fails closed on tag/version mismatch, on an existing release and on a tag that no longer names the built commit, builds and verifies the wheel before publication, publishes an immutable GitHub Release with the wheel and checksums, never cancels a tagged release run for another, and needs no live Claude spend

R9.description: Workers stream stream-json output that is teed to durable per-job logs while preserving the structured final result, classification and reconciliation evidence

R10.description: Operators can observe a running worker live via step/run --follow and attach from another terminal with follow, discovering the active run/job without searching job files

R11.description: Observation is presentation-only and read-only: it changes no command selection, routing, model/effort, permission mode, locking, expected outcome, reconciliation, Workflow state, retry/failure handling or exit code, and a follower detaching never affects the worker

R12.description: status and diagnostics show the active Controller version and runtime identity and the active runs/jobs, with existing exit-code semantics preserved

R13.description: No regression to automatic lifecycle orchestration, locking, routing, review gates or Workflow conformance
